51: Lawyer Joydeep Bhattacharya explained that at the previous hearing on 19 Feb 2021 he had actually been present for Ichhita Dundarwal (A-180) and Neha Kataria (A-181), who are already permanently excused from coming to court, but forgot to sign the attendance sheet. The court accepted this, marked both women as present through their lawyer, and cancelled the fresh court notice that would otherwise have been sent to them. Case kept for 7 May 2021.
52: Ram Lal Arya and Ajit Singh Rathore, who want to switch sides and become witnesses for the prosecution in return for a pardon (approvers), came to court, but their statements were not recorded because SFIO's lawyer asked for more time since the investigating officer was absent and had to study their proposed statements. Their recording was put off till 7 May 2021. Raj Kumar Modi, Surender, Jainam Rathore and Vijay Jindal were shown by video link from jail; other jailed accused held in Jodhpur Jail were not produced, so production orders were issued.
53: Mostly a jail-production hearing. Raj Kumar Modi and Jainam Rathore appeared from jail by video link and Surender was brought to court by jail staff. Vijay Jhindal could not appear because he was admitted in the General Hospital, Gurugram; he is to be shown by video from hospital if possible. Other jailed accused said to be in Jodhpur Jail were again not produced, so fresh production orders were issued and the Jodhpur Jail Superintendent was asked to explain why (show cause notice). Next date 2 April 2021.
54: Several jailed accused were not brought to court. Rajasthan police said Priyanka Modi, Rajeshwar Singh, Vaibhav Lodha, Bharat Das Vaishnav, Rohit Modi, Bharat Modi, Vivek Purohit, Virender Modi and Ishwar Singh Sindal were in police custody (remand) in a Jaipur case (FIR 218/2019, Vidhayakpuri), and Mukesh Kumar Modi and Rahul Virender Modi were on remand in a Jodhpur case (FIR 136/2021). The court asked the Jaipur Jail Superintendent for a detailed explanation, issued a fresh warning notice to the Jodhpur Jail Superintendent for not replying, and ordered production on 16 April 2021. A hospital report on Vijay Jhindal (admitted in General Hospital, Gurugram) was called from the CMO.
55: New judge Phalit Sharma received the case by transfer. Jaipur jail produced Vaibhav, Rohit Modi, Bharat Modi, Rajeshwar Singh, Ishwar Singh, Bharat Dass, Priyanka and Vivek Purohit. Jodhpur jail said Rahul and Mukesh Modi could not be brought because no police escort was available, and apologised. Virender Modi was not produced because jail said he was on interim bail till 17 April 2021, but this court never gave him bail, so the court asked Jodhpur jail to explain why he was let out and ordered all to appear by video on 30 April 2021. Surender was not produced from Bhondsi Jail.
56: Roll-call of jailed accused by video link. Priyanka Modi (women's jail, Jaipur), Rajeshwar, Bharat Modi, Ishwar Singh, Rohit Modi, Vaibhav, Bharat and Vivek Purohit (Central Jail Jaipur) and Vaibhav and Raj Kumar Modi (Bhondsi Jail, Gurugram) appeared by video and were kept in judicial custody. Rahul and Mukesh were not produced from Jodhpur jail and Surender was not produced by Jaipur jail authorities, so production orders were issued. Virender Modi was absent, being on interim bail from the High Court. Next date 20 May 2021.
57: Short adjournment order with nobody present. The file was taken up on the instructions of the District and Sessions Judge, Gurugram (order of 13 May 2021), as the matter was routine in nature. The case was postponed to 8 September 2021 for the purpose already fixed and parties were to be informed. The judge explained the long gap was due to the heavy load of very old cases in his recently joined court that need priority.
58: SFIO asked the court to split off and separately try the accused who had not yet been served (under sections 299/317 CrPC). The court rejected this, saying there was no proof those accused had run away and SFIO seemed to be avoiding its own job of getting them arrested with police help. The judge also scolded court staff and SFIO for not telling him those accused had been summoned, ordered bailable warrants (Rs 5,000 each with one surety) as earlier directed on 19 Feb 2021, and asked police for death reports of Mahender Kumar Tak and Mahesh Kumar Tak.
59: Correction to the same day's order. Because an earlier order of 4 Sep 2019 had already directed arrest, the court ordered arrest warrants (not bailable warrants, which had not worked) against Nitin Rathore, Vinay Kumpawat, Paras Bolia, Manish Chauhary, Deepak Shrimali, Prakash Chandra Purohit, Akshat Singh, Naveen Kumar, Aditya Sarda, Sudhir Punia, Shiv Raj Sharma, Naveen Choudhary, Peeyush Aggarwal, Rajiv Kumar Rana and Sidharth Chauhan, and also against Jinender Vyas, Abhay K. Shah, Shinder Pal Singh, Gurbir Singh Sandhu, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta and Saurabh Tak. Vijay Shukla, Nazima Khan and Shabir Khan to be called through bailable warrants.
60: Raj Kumar Modi was let out of jail on interim bail after the Supreme Court (order of 16 Aug 2021, following the interim bail given to main accused Vivek Harivyasi) allowed it. Conditions: personal bond of Rs 1 lakh with one surety, no foreign travel without permission, surrender passport, no similar business, no tampering with evidence, share phone number and location with SFIO. His wife Rekha Modi stood surety using two ICICI Bank fixed deposits of Rs 50,000 each, which the court kept and informed the bank. Release order sent to jail.
61: Brief adjournment order. Nobody appeared on behalf of the complainant SFIO on this date, and no decision was taken. The judge simply directed that the file be put up on 8 September 2021, the date already fixed in the main case, when the accused were due to appear. Nothing else happened at this hearing.
62: Big roll-call hearing. Customs intelligence (DRI) sought permission to question jailed Jainam Rathore. Mahesh Dutt Sharma excused for today due to a High Court no-arrest assurance; Abhay K. Shah's request to be excused rejected as he never surrendered. Vijay Shukla appeared under Supreme Court no-arrest protection. Ten accused who became approvers (prosecution witnesses for pardon) to give statements, starting with Ajit Singh and Ram Lal Arya on 17 Sep 2021. Arrest warrants for Nazima Khan and Shabbir Khan for dodging; fresh arrest warrants for about 22 others, with absconding proceedings to be considered. Surender in hospital; Vijay Kumar Jhindal reported dead.
63: Short adjournment order. Only SFIO's senior public prosecutor Hari Kishan was present. At his request, the case was postponed to 15 September 2021 for arguments on an application filed by DRI (the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, a customs and revenue investigation agency). No other decision was taken on this date.
64: Brief cover order on Sudhir Mehta's application in the SFIO case. His lawyer Neeraj Dev Gaur and SFIO's prosecutors were present. SFIO filed its reply, arguments were heard, and the court dismissed Sudhir Mehta's application by a separate detailed order passed the same day (his request to cancel the arrest warrant against him). Papers were attached to the main case file and the order was pronounced in open court.
65: Sudhir Mehta (A-170) of Udaipur asked the court to cancel the arrest warrant against him, citing Supreme Court rulings (Aman Preet Singh, Siddharth) that arrest is not always needed. SFIO argued he had hidden the fact that his anticipatory bail plea was still pending in the High Court and that the Companies Act, a special law, applies. The court rejected his request, mainly because he concealed the pending High Court case (fixed for 1 Nov 2021), and because without a High Court stay on arrest it could not interfere. Arrest warrant stays.
66: Short adjournment order. Only the senior special public prosecutor Satish Aggarwala, appearing for DRI (the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, a customs and revenue investigation agency) officer Shailendra Singh Bhadauria, was present. At his request, DRI's application was listed for arguments on 17 September 2021. No decision was taken on this date.
67: Raj Kumar Bohra (A-171), a chartered accountant and NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and children live in Dubai, asked for general permission to travel abroad. He had travelled to UAE, Bangladesh and Dubai earlier with permission and always returned on time. SFIO opposed only half-heartedly. The court allowed him to travel to UAE from 14 Sep 2021 and return before 23 Dec 2021, on condition he gives property or bank guarantee security of Rs 1 crore (forfeited if he misuses it) and follows his travel plan.
68: Short adjournment on Rajeev Kumar Rana's (A-177) application to cancel the non-bailable arrest warrant against him and to be excused from appearing in court in person. SFIO's prosecutors filed their reply to the application. His lawyers Ajit Sharma and Aakash Jangra asked for time to argue, which the court allowed. The case was fixed for arguments on 22 September 2021.
69: Customs intelligence (DRI) was allowed to question accused Jainam Madhukant Rathod alias Jainam Jain, in jail since 28 Aug 2019, in its separate customs-duty evasion probe involving M/s Shivani Network. The court directed Bhondsi District Jail, Gurugram to let Senior Intelligence Officer Shailendra Singh Bhadauria and officers Ishu Kumar Verma and Anirudh Singh Bhati visit on 21 Sep 2021 with their files to record his statement under section 108 of the Customs Act.
70: Ajit Singh (A-150) and Ram Lal Arya (A-158) came to court to give their statements about becoming approvers (switching sides to be prosecution witnesses in return for a pardon), but the court ran out of time. Their statements were postponed to 14 October 2021 and both were told to appear in person.
71: Brief order on Rajeev Kumar Rana's (A-177) application to cancel the non-bailable arrest warrant against him and be excused from appearing in court in person. His lawyers Ajit Sharma and Aakash Jangra and SFIO's prosecutors argued the matter. The court dismissed the application by a separate detailed order the same day, so the arrest warrant against him stays. Papers attached to the main file.
72: Detailed ruling rejecting Rajeev Kumar Rana's (A-177) request to cancel his non-bailable arrest warrant and excuse him from appearing. He argued that since SFIO never arrested him during the investigation, which he cooperated with, Supreme Court rulings (Siddharth, Aman Preet Singh) mean he should not be arrested now. The court held that fraud under the Companies Act is a special law with strict bail conditions (section 212(6)), relying on High Court rulings in Jainam Rathod and Vijay Shukla cases, and called the request a disguised attempt to get bail. His anticipatory bail had earlier been refused. Arrest warrant stays.
73: Ajit Singh (A-150) and Ram Lal Arya (A-158) again came to court to give their statements about becoming approvers (switching sides to be prosecution witnesses in return for a pardon), but the judge was on half-day casual leave and no court time was left. Their statements were put off to 23 December 2021, the date already fixed in the case, and both were told to come in person.
74: Surender Singh was let out of jail on interim bail after the Supreme Court (order of 29 Oct 2021) noted he became director seven years after the company took the loan, co-accused already had interim bail, and he had been in jail since 2019. Conditions: Rs 1 lakh personal bond and surety, no foreign travel without permission, no similar business, no tampering with evidence, share phone and location with SFIO. His surety deposited Rs 1 lakh cash, to be swapped for a fixed deposit. Jail told not to release him until he deposits his passport with the Supreme Court registry.
75: Short adjournment order with nobody present. Because the judge was going to be on casual leave from 20 to 23 December 2021, the case was taken up early, on 15 December 2021, and postponed to 25 March 2022 for the same purpose already fixed. All concerned were to be informed of the new date. No other decision was taken.
76: Priyanka Modi was let out on bail after the Supreme Court ordered her release on 7 Feb 2022 (Criminal Appeal arising from SLP 301 of 2022), which court staff confirmed. She furnished a personal bond of Rs 1 lakh with one surety, and a release order was issued to the jail. A fixed deposit given as surety was frozen: the State Bank of India branch at Bhagat Ki Kothi, Krishi Upaj Mandi, Jodhpur was told not to cash it without court permission. Next date 6 April 2022.
77: 24 wanted accused to be declared absconding; notices put up publicly (they become 'proclaimed persons' if absent on 2 July 2022) against Nitin Rathore, Jinender Vyas, Vinay Kumpawat, Paras Bolia, Abhay K. Shah, Manish Chaudhary, Deepak Shrimali, Prakash Chandra Purohit, Sidharth Chauhan, Akshat Singh, Shinder Pal Singh, Gurbir Singh Sandhu, Naveen Kumar, Aditya Sarda, Sudhir Punia, Nazima Khan, Shabir Khan, Shiv Raj Sharma, Naveen Chaudhary, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta, Saurabh Tak, Peeyush Aggarwal and Rajeev Kumar Rana after warrants since 2019 failed. Cases of dead accused Mahender Kumar Tak and Vijay Kumar Jindal closed. Warrants for Mahesh Kumar Tak; arrest warrants for Neha Gemawat and Meenakshi Modi.
78: Approver statements recorded. Ten accused granted bail by the High Court on condition they cooperate as approvers (switching sides to become prosecution witnesses in return for a pardon) came to court. The statements on oath of Hemant Kumar, Ajit Singh Rathore, Smt. Damyanti and Ram Lal Arya were recorded and the court allowed these four to become approvers. Because court time ran out, the remaining six (Jitesh Kumar, Shashank Shekhar, Dushyant Singh, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Parveen Kumar, Ritu Raj Singh) were called for 7 May 2022.
79: Jainam Rathod (Jainum Rathore) was let out of jail on bail after the Supreme Court ordered his release on 18 April 2022 (Criminal Appeal 640 of 2022). Link Judge Jasbir Singh handled it as the regular judge was on leave. He furnished a personal bond of Rs 1 lakh with one surety and a release order was sent to the jail. The surety's fixed deposit was frozen, with Bank of India, Connaught Circus branch told not to cash it without court permission. Next date 7 May 2022.
80: On SFIO's request, the court ordered that Rajeev Kumar Rana (A-177), a wanted accused against whom proceedings to declare him absconding were under way, be brought from District Jail, Jaipur, where he is held. The Jaipur jail superintendent was directed to produce him by video link if possible on 7 May 2022, or otherwise in person in custody, so that he can be taken into custody in this case in which he had been wanted for a long time.
81: Police officers who served the public 'wanted' proclamation notices gave statements confirming publication against about 22 absconding accused, including Gurbir Singh Sandhu, Shinder Pal Singh, Sidharth Chauhan, Nitin Rathore, Sudhir Mehta, Nazima Khan and Shabbir Khan; they must appear on 2 July 2022. Rajiv Kumar Rana was reported to be in custody in Jaipur, so a production order was issued. The officer for Akshat Singh did not come. Aditya Sharda's request to be excused and Nitin Rathore's request to stop the absconding proceedings were both rejected. Approver Dushyant Singh Rathore's statement was recorded; other approvers' statements postponed.
82: Short procedural order. SFIO applied for a public proclamation (absconding notice) to be issued against accused Akshat Singh. The court received a report from its own clerk (Ahlmad) and called for a report from the clerk of Judge Phalit Sharma's court, which had earlier handled the case, for 11 May 2022.
83: The court found that the proclamation (public 'wanted' notice) against Akshat Singh (A-136), ordered on 25 March 2022, was never actually issued because court constable Ct. Satish Kumar, attached to Judge Phalit Sharma's court, withheld or destroyed the notice given to him on 30 April 2022. A fresh proclamation was ordered, to be published by 25 May 2022, with the constable who serves it to testify on 30 May. Since the matter was already sent to the Gurugram Police Commissioner for inquiry, the court took no further action but asked that the inquiry finish within three months.
84: Short hearing. The public proclamation (absconding notice) against Akshat Singh (A-136) had been put up and the report was filed. But the serving officer, EHC Gajraj, did not appear to give his statement because he fell ill and went to Civil Hospital, Gurugram; a copy of his prescription was placed on record. Case put up on 2 June 2022 for his statement.
85: New judge Dr. Virender Parshad received the case by transfer. EHC Gajraj, the officer who served the absconding notice against Akshat Singh, again did not appear due to his treatment, so the matter was adjourned to 7 June 2022. Meenakshi Modi and Neha Ghemawat Modi asked that arrest warrants not be issued because the Supreme Court had on 20 May 2022 stayed the Rajasthan High Court's order. The court agreed: no arrest warrants against them, and any already issued to be recalled unexecuted.
86: EHC Gajraj Singh, the police officer who put up the public proclamation (absconding notice) against Akshat Singh (A-136), gave his statement confirming it was affixed. Later the same day Akshat Singh's lawyer, Amol Gupta, filed an application asking the court to drop or pause the absconding proceedings against him. A copy was given to SFIO and the case was fixed for 2 July 2022 for the accused's presence and for SFIO's reply on that application.
87: Big roll-call hearing under new judge Dr. Virender Parshad. Absconding proceedings against most of the 24 wanted accused (e.g. Nitin Rathore, Abhay K. Shah, Jinender Vyas, Sudhir Mehta, Rajiv Kumar Rana) were paused till 30 Aug 2022 on High Court orders; also paused for Akshat Singh, Naveen Kumar and Shiv Raj Sharma (who seeks to become an approver). Vinay Kumawat, Sidharth Chauhan and Sudhir Punia did not appear despite proclamation; decision deferred to 27 July. Raj Kumar Bohra sought foreign travel; Megha Chauhan sought her passport back to renew her child's passport. Mahesh Kumar Tak's arrest warrant reissued.
88: Megha Chauhan asked for her passport, kept in the court record, to be returned so she could show it to the passport office to renew the passport of her minor child, Yashas. SFIO did not file a reply but asked that she return it within a fixed time. The court found the reason genuine and released the passport on a Rs 50,000 personal bond with one surety, on condition she returns it within one month, files a certified copy first, and does not leave India without the court's permission.
89: Raj Kumar Bohra, an NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and three children live in Dubai and who runs RKC International General Trading LLC in UAE with export business in Bangladesh, asked permission to travel abroad. SFIO gave no objection. Noting he had travelled abroad with permission before and always returned, the court allowed him to travel after 3 July 2022 and come back before 30 Aug 2022, on condition he gives Rs 1 crore security by property or bank guarantee (forfeited if misused) and follows his itinerary.
90: Short order. Naveen Kumar, who had been granted bail by this court on 19 July 2022 in bail application BA-4346-2022, filed his bail bonds through his lawyer Abhimanyu Dhawan. The court accepted and attested the bonds, attached the papers to the main case file, and kept the case for 27 July 2022, the date and purpose already fixed.
91: First page only of the 27 July 2022 hearing, listing attendance. Approvers on bail, including Ajit Singh Rathore, Ramlal Arya, Parveen Kumar, Nimesh Kumar Ramesh Soni, Ritu Raj Singh, Shashank and Dushyant Singh Rathore, Jitesh Kumar Parmar and Damyanti Bhandari, appeared in person. Hemant Kumar Jain, Akshat Singh, Shiv Raj Sharma and Naveen Kumar were represented by lawyers. Mukesh Modi (moved to Hanumangarh jail) and others moved to Jodhpur jail were not produced by Jaipur jail, and Mahesh Kumar Tak was absent.
92: Vinay Kumawat and Sudhir Punia were formally declared 'proclaimed persons' (officially absconding) after failing to appear despite public notices; police and DCP Gurugram told to act against them under section 174-A IPC. Sidharth Chauhan's declaration was postponed because his High Court petition is pending, and Shiv Raj Sharma's paused pending his High Court plea to become an approver. Peeyush Aggarwal's wife Anupama said he would surrender within a week, so he was given time. Akshat Singh and Naveen Kumar had got bail. Rajiv Kumar Rana, shown by video from Jaipur jail, was taken into custody in this case.
93: Short adjournment order. Because the case has 187 accused represented by many lawyers, checking and uploading the detailed order of the day would take time, so by this short order the case was adjourned to 18 October 2022 and 29 November 2022. No other decisions are recorded in this short order.
94: Raj Kumar Bohra, an NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and three children live in Dubai, and who runs a trading business in UAE with exports to Bangladesh, was again allowed to travel abroad after 30 Aug 2022 and must return before 18 Oct 2022. SFIO gave no objection. Conditions: Rs 1 crore security by property or bank guarantee (forfeited if misused) and strict travel itinerary. His surety Ajay Kumar Arora, who had already given Rs 1 crore security, agreed by affidavit to continue and to produce him on the next date.
95: Detailed roll-call hearing. Rajiv Kumar Rana appeared by video and stays in custody; Mukesh Modi now moved to Barmer jail. Vinay Kumawat and Sudhir Punia already declared absconding with action under section 174-A. Absconding proceedings against Sidharth Chauhan, Nitin Rathore, Abhay K. Shah and about 17 others stay paused on High Court orders. Peeyush Aggarwal's proclamation put on hold because he filed anticipatory bail. Several accused excused for the day, including Aditya Sarda, Megha Chauhan, Indu Tak and Shiv Raj Sharma. Neha Kataria sought permanent exemption; Meenakshi Modi and Neha Ghemawat Modi sought exemption pending Rajasthan High Court case. Approver statements set for 18 Oct 2022.
96: Short adjournment order. Because the case has 187 accused represented by many lawyers, checking and uploading the detailed order of the day would take time, so by this short order the case was adjourned to 9 December 2022, the date already fixed. No other decisions are recorded in this short order.
97: Raj Kumar Bohra, an NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and three children live in Dubai and who runs RKC International General Trading LLC in UAE with exports to Bangladesh, was again allowed to travel abroad after 18 Oct 2022 and must return before 9 Dec 2022. SFIO gave no objection. Conditions: Rs 1 crore security by property or bank guarantee (forfeited if misused) and strict travel itinerary. Surety Ajay Kumar Arora, who already gave Rs 1 crore security, agreed to continue and produce him, and his statement was recorded separately.
98: Detailed roll-call hearing. Rajiv Kumar Rana could not be shown by video because the video link had a technical fault; Mahesh Kumar Tak's arrest warrant came back unserved, so a fresh one was issued with a note that the serving officer must explain any failure. 99: Short adjournment order. Because the case has 187 accused represented by many lawyers, checking and uploading the detailed order of the day would take time, so by this short order the case was adjourned to 8 February 2023, the date already fixed. No other decisions are recorded in this short order.
100: Detailed roll-call hearing. Rajiv Kumar Rana again not shown by video due to a technical fault. No coercive action against Mahesh Kumar Tak or Shiv Raj Sharma since their bail applications are now pending in this court. The High Court refused Piyush (Peeyush) Aggarwal's anticipatory bail on 8 Dec 2022 and told him to surrender within a week, so the court will wait for him. Priyanka Modi excused on medical grounds; Ajit Singh, Megha, Damyanti Bhandari, Indu Tak, Raj Kumar Bohra and Ichita also excused.
